terms.meaning: The two-headed imaginary bird that was the Wodeyars' royal emblem.
Chikkadevaraja's central office in the capital, with 18 departments.
An official who ran Mysore's government in the king's name when the kings were weak.
The British handing Mysore back to Chamaraja Wodeyar X in 1881.
A small chieftain under Vijayanagara; his territory was a Paleyapattu.
Land revenue fixed by land class (fertility, irrigation), at one-third of the gross produce.
The Nizam's 53 rules that took away people's basic freedoms.

items.name: Chikkadevaraja Wodeyar (1673-1704)
items.formula: Set up the Athara Kacheri, fixed weights and measures, began a postal system, dammed the Kaveri near Srirangapattana.
items.example: He leased Bengaluru from the Mughals for three lakh varahas and was called "Navakoti Narayana".

items.name: Writers in Chikkadevaraja's court
items.formula: Singararya wrote Mitravinda-govinda, the first Kannada drama.
items.example: Sanchi Honnamma wrote Hadibadeya Dharma.

items.name: Hyder Ali (1761-1782)
items.formula: A commander under Dalavayi Nanjarajayya who took power as Karyakarta, setting aside Krishnaraja Wodeyar II.
items.example: Illiterate but able, he doubled Mysore's territory and started the Lalbagh.

items.name: First and Second Mysore wars
items.formula: First (1767-1769): British lost and signed the treaty of Madras. Second (1780-1784): Hyder died; Tippu ended it with the Mangaluru treaty.
items.example: Hyder fought the second because the British didn't help him against the Marathas.

items.name: Third and Fourth Mysore wars
items.formula: Third (1790-1792): Tippu gave up half his kingdom, paid indemnity and gave two sons as hostages. Fourth (1799): he died at Srirangapattana.
items.example: His kingdom was then split four ways.

items.name: Achievements of Tippu Sultan
items.formula: Spread sericulture, modernised the army with French help, used rockets, gave grants to temples and Shringeri Math.
items.example: He built Dariya Doulath and the Jumma Masjid at Srirangapattana, with mints there and at Bengaluru.

items.name: Krishnaraja Wodeyar III
items.formula: Put on the throne at five, with Poornaiah as Diwan.
items.example: He was removed after the Bidanuru revolt, and commissioners ruled (1831-1881).

items.name: Mark Cubbon (1834-1861)
items.formula: Moved the capital to Bengaluru, made districts and taluks, made Kannada the official language.
items.example: The state's first railway, Bengaluru to Jolarpet, began in 1859.

items.name: Bowring and Chamaraja Wodeyar X
items.formula: Bowring (1862-1870) reformed revenue and set up Public Instruction. Chamaraja Wodeyar X ruled from the 1881 Rendition.
items.example: The People's Representative Assembly began in 1881; Diwans: Rangacharlu and Sheshadri Iyer.

items.name: Naalvadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar (1902-1940)
items.formula: Gave J. N. Tata 371 acres for a science institute, set up the Legislative Assembly (1907), built the KRS dam, gave women the vote.
items.example: Gandhiji called his Mysore "Ramarajya" and him "Rajyashri".

items.name: Sir M. Vishveshwaraiah (Diwan 1912-1918)
items.formula: "Industrialization or Destruction": Bhadravathi iron works, Mysuru Bank (1913), Kannada Sahitya Parishad (1915), Mysuru University (1916).
items.example: First Kannadiga to get the Bharatha Ratna, in 1955.

items.name: Sir Mirza Ismail (Diwan 1926-1941)
items.formula: HAL, glass and porcelain factories in Bengaluru, Mandya sugar factory, Irwin Canal, Brindavan Garden.
items.example: NIMHANS and other hospitals were started in his time.

items.name: Mysore joins India
items.formula: K. C. Reddy's Palace Satyagraha; a responsible government on 24 October 1947.
items.example: Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar became the first Governor and K. C. Reddy the first Chief Minister.

items.name: Hiriya Venkatappa Nayaka
items.formula: Made Keladi independent; beat the Portuguese at Mangaluru with Abbakka of Ullala.
items.example: He set up a victory pillar at Hanagal after beating the Adil Shahis.

items.name: Shivappa Nayaka
items.formula: Took Portuguese ports, title "Padugadalodeya"; built forts at Bekal and Chandragiri.
items.example: He welcomed Goan traders and Christians and gave them land.

items.name: Rani Chennammaji of Keladi
items.formula: Shivappa Nayaka's daughter-in-law; sheltered Shivaji's son Rajaram from the Mughals.
items.example: She gave land for a church in Mangaluru; Hyder finally took Keladi.

items.name: Madakari Nayaka and Obavva
items.formula: Chitradurga's greatest Nayaka, king at twelve; Hyder's first siege failed when Obavva killed the intruders at the secret path.
items.example: Hyder later won; the fort has seven walls.

items.name: Kempegowda I and II
items.formula: I: founded Bengaluru, built its fort and the Kempambudhi, Dharmambudhi, Halasuru and Sampangi lakes.
items.example: II: built four watch towers at Bengaluru's limits; the family later ruled from Magadi.

items.name: Kodagu's history
items.formula: The Haleri dynasty (founded by Veeraraja); Mudduraja made Muddurajakeri (Madikeri) the capital.
items.example: The British took Kodagu in 1834 and exiled Chikkaveera Rajendra.

items.name: Amarasullia revolt (1837)
items.formula: Farmers rose against heavy land tax and held Sullia, Puttur, Kasaragod and Mangaluru for thirteen days.
items.example: Leaders: Puttabasappa, Kalyanaswami, Guddemane Appayya Gowda.

items.name: Two great soldiers of Kodagu
items.formula: Field Marshal K. M. Cariappa, first Indian General and chief of independent India's forces.
items.example: General K. S. Thimayya led India to victory against Pakistan. Kodagu joined Karnataka in 1956.

items.name: Rani Chennamma of Kittur
items.formula: Collector Thackeray called her adopted son's claim illegal; she fought, and Thackeray was killed.
items.example: Betrayed later, she was imprisoned at Bailhongal; she was the first Indian woman to oppose British rule.

items.name: Sangolli Rayanna
items.formula: Chennamma's follower who fought a guerrilla war against the British.
items.example: Captured by traitors and hanged; a banyan tree grows on his grave at Nandagada.

items.name: Tulunadu
items.formula: Today's Dakshina Kannada and Udupi; long ruled by the Alupas; Abbakka of Ullala beat the Portuguese.
items.example: Naga and Bhuta worship; Madhvacharya came from here; Kittel's Kannada dictionary was printed at the Basel Mission Press.

items.name: Tulunadu's freedom fighters
items.formula: Karnad Sadashiva Rao, the "Deshabhakta"; Attavar Yellappa, a minister in Netaji's Azad Hind Fauz.
items.example: Kudmul Ranga Rao worked against untouchability; Canara, Corporation, Syndicate and Vijaya Banks began here.

items.name: Revolt of the Halagali Bedas (1857)
items.formula: The Bedanayakas refused the Arms Act's demand for permission to keep arms.
items.example: 290 were captured and 19 hanged; Rami shot three soldiers and died a martyr.

items.name: Sindhura Lakshmana
items.formula: Took from the rich and the British treasury and gave to the poor.
items.example: He was shot dead by the British; his tomb is at Bilagi.

items.name: Naalvadi Venkatappa Nayaka of Surapura
items.formula: Planned to unite South Indian kings against the British in 1857; Surapura fell in 1858.
items.example: Betrayed by Salar Jung, he was shot on the way to exile; twelve Nayakas ruled Surapura from 1636.

items.name: Liberation of Hyderabad-Karnataka
items.formula: Leaders: Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Hardikar Manjappa ("Gandhi of Karnataka"), Vande Mataram Ramachandra Rao, Sharanagowda Inamdar ("Sardar").
items.example: The Indian Army entered on 17 September 1948 and the Nizam surrendered.

mistakes.text: Rani Chennamma fought at Kittur; Rani Chennammaji ruled Keladi. They are two different queens.
Vishveshwaraiah was Diwan from 1912 to 1918; Mirza Ismail later, from 1926 to 1941. Both served Naalvadi.
Hyder Ali started the Lalbagh; Kempegowda II's watch tower stands there.
